This Psalm probably relates to the captivity of the ten tribes, as the former to that of Judah. Its complaint is aggravated by the contrast of former prosperity, and the prayer for relief occurs as a refrain through the Psalm. 1-2. Joseph-- for Ephraim ( 1Ch 7:20-29 ; Psa 78:67 ; Re 7:8 ), for Israel. Shepherd-- (Compare Ge 49:24 ). leadest, &c.-- ( Psa 77:20 ). dwellest ... cherubim-- ( Ex 25:20 ); the place of God's visible glory, whence He communed with the people ( He 9:5 ). shine forth-- appear ( Psa 50:2 ; 94:1 ).
